name: Cone photoreceptor electrical response to light
summary: Absorbed light drives the cone phototransduction cascade, closing cGMP-gated cation channels and hyperpolarizing the photoreceptor membrane. The downstream electrical response does not reproduce the optical carrier frequency.

axis.notes: Electrical response after phototransduction; the optical carrier frequency is not preserved as an electrical oscillation.

constraints: graded transient response rather than a copy of the optical carrier
spectral content depends on stimulus timing, adaptation state, and retinal physiology

mechanisms.description: Photon absorption activates the photopigment/transducin/PDE cascade, lowers cGMP, closes cGMP-gated cation channels, and hyperpolarizes the photoreceptor.

source_ref.label: Incident optical stimulus at a cone photoreceptor

relationships.description: Incident photons are physically transduced by the cone phototransduction cascade into a graded electrical membrane response. The CIE LMS curve remains a descriptive response model, not the physical source node.
Light-induced photoreceptor hyperpolarization reduces transmitter release at the photoreceptor synapse.

sources.title: Phototransduction
sources.publisher: NCBI Bookshelf, National Library of Medicine

evidence.derivation: The source describes a biochemical transduction cascade producing a graded membrane-potential response; Atlas therefore does not assign the optical carrier frequency to the electrical output.
